# Ezekiel 19 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 19:7 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-he-knew their-widows, and-their-cities he-laid-waste; and-the-land and-its-fullness was-appalled at-the-sound-of his-roaring. |
| LOGOS | and seized their widows. He laid waste their cities, and the land was appalled and all who were in it at the sound of his roaring. |
| PNEUMA | He attacked their strongholds and devastated their cities. The entire land and everyone in it was terrified by his roaring. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 19:13 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-now she-is-planted in-the-wilderness, in-a-land-of drought and-thirst. |
| LOGOS | Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land. |
| PNEUMA | Now she is planted in the desert — in a dry, parched land. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 19:8 (overlap: 5%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-the-nations set against-him from-the-provinces all-around, and-they-spread over-him their-net; in-their-pit he-was-caught. |
| LOGOS | Then the nations set against him from provinces on every side; they spread their net over him; he was taken in their pit. |
| PNEUMA | So the nations from surrounding lands set a trap for him. They spread their net over him, and he fell into their pit. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 19:14 (overlap: 6%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-fire went-out from-a-rod-of her-branches, [and]-consumed her-fruit, and-there-is-not in-her a-branch-of strength, a-scepter for-ruling.' It [is] a-lament, and-it-became a-lament." |
| LOGOS | And fire has gone out from its stem, has consumed its fruit, so that there remains in it no strong stem, no scepter for ruling. This is a lamentation and has become a lamentation." |
| PNEUMA | Fire has spread from her own stem and burned up her branches and fruit. No strong branch remains — no scepter to rule with. This is a funeral song, and it is meant to be sung as one." |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 19:12 (overlap: 7%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | But-she-was-plucked-up in-fury, to-the-ground she-was-cast-down, and-the-east wind dried-up her-fruit; they-were-broken-off and-withered — her-branch-of strength — fire consumed-it. |
| LOGOS | But the vine was plucked up in fury, cast down to the ground; the east wind dried up its fruit; its strong stems were broken off and withered; the fire consumed them. |
| PNEUMA | But she was ripped up in fury and thrown to the ground. The scorching east wind dried up all her fruit. Her strong branches broke off and withered, and fire consumed them. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 19:5 (overlap: 9%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-she-saw that she-waited, her-hope was-lost, and-she-took another of-her-cubs — a-young-lion she-made-him. |
| LOGOS | When she saw that she waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion. |
| PNEUMA | When the mother lion saw that her hopes for that cub were gone, she took another cub and trained him to be a young lion. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.
